sources.citation: Krishan, Shree. 2001. A sketch of Raji grammar. In Y. Nagano & R. J. LaPolla (eds.), New Research on Zhangzhung and Related Himalayan Languages (Senri Ethnological Reports 19), 449-497. Osaka: National Museum of Ethnology. [Raji of Pithoragarh = Glottolog rawa1264]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number Loeb Music Library.69.80.1.4 (19)); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number MUS.69.80.1.4 (19)
sources.note: Phonology sec. 2.0-2.2 (pp. 451-458): 33 consonants, 7 vowels; sec. 2.0.3 'Suprasegmental' lists only 'Nasalization'; 2.2 syllable structure. No statement on stress or accent anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent: zero hits).

sources.citation: Fortier, Jana & Kavita Rastogi. 2004. Sister languages? Comparative phonology of two Himalayan languages [Khaamci/Raute and Rawati/Raji]. Nepalese Linguistics 21: 42-52.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'Phonological impressions': Raji (Rawati) c. 24 consonants, 7 vowels, sporadic nasalization; a tone remark only for Khaamci (Raute: 'long geminate vowels with falling tones in word final position'). No stress statement for Raji/Rawati.
